newsitem.title: ITALY: Versace updates mini, shoulder pad muscles back.
newsitem.headline: Versace updates mini, shoulder pad muscles back.

text.p: Thoroughly modern minis swung jauntily down the catwalk in top Italian designer Gianni Versace's autumn/winter collection on Saturday in a show that sent shoulder pads edging back into vogue.
Versace, parading his 1997/98 ready-to-wear collection on the penultimate day of the Milan shows, displayed a glittering and glamorous range of evening wear.

Sparkling square-necked bikini-style tops in such two-tone combinations as gold and black and gold and red and others incorporating greens, blues and aquamarine went with matching straight mini skirts in a light supple material.
High-waisted day and evening minidresses, some strapless, others with a different hued fabric attached like a tiny, filmy jacket at the chest, were worn over knee-high boots with stiletto heels.
Short black skirts had panels cut out behind to reveal a flash of flesh just below the waistband or on the hip bone.
Colours were characteristically bold, with limes, lacquer red and turquoise or intenser burgundies, dark greens and black. Leather was black, with thigh-length belted jackets worn over tiny minis.

But skirts did not just stop at the thigh. Mid-calf and longer garments featured while jackets, some cut like dinner jackets, had a faintly masculine outline by returning to padded shoulders but without the sharp aggression of the 1980s.
Versace said in a statement the designs were for women looking for quality and he wasn't giving a fashion ultimatum or a "violent statement so often expressed in fashion".

Fashion house Moschino gave a bouncy show with skirts, jackets and trousers decorated at the front with anti-nuclear peace signs, all done in a rich palette of warm reds, purples and blues, and then left white in the background like a painted sheet.

Skirts were mostly ankle length with an early 20th century flavour from layers of velvet, lace and crocheting as well as from the long silhouette which was generous over the hips and thighs and then appeared to taper in again towards the foot.
Shoes were high-heeled and models wore a selection of cloche-like bonnets and knitted wool hats with small brims turned up at the front.
Daywear included broad-legged trousers and jackets with padded but not excessive shoulders, with an overall flavour of country tweeds and checks set off by tweedy peaked caps.

For evening the profile was mostly long and some dresses were straight to the knee, stopping at a horizontal band and then resuming again with a different, silky fabric to give a voluminous section down to the ankle.
An eye-catching series of trousers, skirts and jackets were dyed at the hem in orange and red to create the appearance of flames rising up into a midnight blue sky.
The eight days of shows close on Sunday with the primary line of Giorgio Armani as the final presentation.
